items.title: Who Is Alice Huang, the Woman in the Middle of Nvidia’s Spy Scandal?
items.summary: Alice Huang, who U.S. intelligence determined is a Chinese asset, emerged from the high-flying world of Shanghai finance to work with tech titans and obtain essential A.I. chips.

items.title: Nvidia’s Board Has a History of Letting Jensen Huang Get His Way
items.summary: Governance experts question whether the board, which is investigating Mr. Huang’s conduct, has been too deferential as he has turned Nvidia into a global giant.

items.title: Elevated Inflation Keeps Pressure on Fed to Raise Rates
items.summary: October’s Consumer Price Index report showed a broadening of price pressures that has stoked concerns about the Federal Reserve’s grip on inflation.

items.title: Data Show Households Still Managing to Meet Their Monthly Debts
items.summary: The New York Fed detailed general steadiness in debt payments for autos, student loans and mortgages.

items.title: Oil Prices Have Tumbled in November. Here’s Why.
items.summary: The global benchmark price is down more than $20 a barrel since late October, when it traded for around $113.

items.title: Failure of California Billionaire Tax Strikes Blow to Progressive Agenda
items.summary: A wealth tax on billionaires seemed like a political layup. The outcome of a California ballot initiative shows otherwise.

items.title: In Midterm Elections, Voters Backed Democrats but Broke Right on Many Ballot Measures
items.summary: Many Republican and moderate voters who chose Democratic candidates did not do the same on transgender and other social issues.

items.title: Anthropic Targets Valuation of Up to $1.4 Trillion for Blockbuster I.P.O.
items.summary: The A.I. company’s pricing would make it one of the biggest ever public listings. It comes at a volatile moment in markets, with investors questioning the sustainability of the A.I. boom.

items.title: You May All Go to Hell, and Tommy Lee Jones Will Go to Texas
items.summary: The private actor enjoys life with his horses in the Texas Hill Country, removed from the show-business fray. But he’s back on TV for the first time in decades, in “The Lowdown.”

items.title: The Impeachment Charges Against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, Explained
items.summary: The charges accuse the defense secretary of illegally starting the war with Iran, directing extrajudicial killings and ignoring laws meant to minimize civilian casualties.

items.title: Americans across the economic spectrum feel a 'panic' about finances, author says
items.summary: Mona Chalabi spent five years following Americans living paycheck to paycheck, as well as those earning top wages. Her new book, Ten Lives, explores why financial security can feel so elusive.

items.title: Gas prices dip below $4 but inflation remains stubbornly high
items.summary: Gasoline prices fell below $4 a gallon Tuesday for the first time in three months — but the overall cost of living remains stubbornly high.

items.title: 'Like gods reigning over humans': Many defectors see daughter of North Korea's Kim as heir apparent
items.summary: Little is known about her except that she's reportedly about 13 and named Kim Ju Ae, but Korea's spy agency says she's likely her father's heir.

items.title: Indonesia's VP offers resignation as questions mount over his eligibility
items.summary: His resignation offer comes amid a widening political rift between Prabowo and Widodo and a separate investigation into allegations that senior police officials wiretapped the president.

items.title: The average cost for a new vehicle in the U.S. hits a record high: over $51,000
items.summary: Vehicle transaction prices are up to a new record high, according to the Kelley Blue Book — and some buyers are extending their car loans to finance them.

items.title: Seven days of chaos in the ER: How this country's healthcare system is unraveling
items.summary: Renewed fighting has pushed Ethiopia's healthcare system close to collapse: "The whole emergency (room) was flooded with war trauma patients," one surgeon says of a brutal week in September.

items.title: Get in, loser: Broadway's newest 'Mean Girls' are ready to insult (and enlighten) you
items.summary: "School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play," is ending a Broadway run this week and celebrating with livestream broadcasts. We interviewed the Tony-nominated playwright, Jocelyn Bioh.

items.title: House set to vote to impeach Hegseth. And, SCOTUS allows border wall work to proceed
items.summary: The House could vote to impeach Hegseth, but removing him from office will be tough. And, SCOTUS ruled that a federal judge did not have the authority to halt border wall construction.

items.title: Why did California's billionaire tax fail to surf the blue wave?
items.summary: Two economists debate what California's vote on Prop 40 means for the wealth tax movement.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine hold nearly 4 hours of U.S.-mediated talks in Abu Dhabi
items.summary: Hopes of progress in ending Europe's biggest conflict since World War II are tempered by the absence of any significant breakthroughs in three previous rounds of talks early this year.

items.title: Indigenous-led group receives Cape Cod plot taken from Native Americans centuries ago
items.summary: The Native Land Conservancy is taking over a plot of land that was taken centuries ago and plans to protect it.

items.title: Inflation pace slowed in October, but prices remain high
items.summary: Falling gas prices contributed to the slower increase in prices, but food prices picked up.

items.title: Cockpit voice recorder recovered from Florida jet crash that killed 9
items.summary: The voice recorder was found at the site where the Bahamas-bound plane crashed on Nov. 1, investigators said.

items.title: At least 19 ICE recruits named in DHS hack were hired despite red flags
items.summary: A Post review of records exposed in a DHS hack found that some immigration officers quickly hired last year were involved in past misconduct or criminality.

items.title: Supreme Court allows major part of Trump’s border security project in Texas
items.summary: The more than 500-mile stretch of road, cameras, vehicle barriers and sensors is planned in and around Big Bend National Park. It is one of the longest sections.

items.title: Supreme Court seems likely to limit prisoners’ ability to sue over claims of poor medical care
items.summary: The justices did not seem ready to overturn a 1971 precedent that let individuals harmed by federal officers in violation of their constitutional rights sue for monetary damages.

items.title: Pat Summitt, Willie Mays, unicorns featured on new postage stamps
items.summary: The 2027 collection is to spotlight “sports legends, mythical creatures and celebrations.”

items.title: New Jersey town loses $26 million in ‘sophisticated financial theft’
items.summary: Officials investigating the incident have so far identified $17.3 million they say has been “successfully frozen.”

items.title: FDA tells GLP-1 makers to warn of potential vision loss side effect
items.summary: The agency is requiring GLP-1 manufacturers to warn the drugs can increase risk of “eye stroke.”

items.title: Post-midterm DOJ leadership shake-up continues
items.summary: There has been significant personnel churn and an overhaul of priorities at the Justice Department in President Donald Trump’s second term.
